root_cause.text: The CAN USB ems_usb driver incorrectly assumed receive URBs remained on dev->rx_submitted across completion/resubmission, but the USB core unanchors an URB before ems_usb_read_bulk_callback(), so resubmitted RX URBs were no longer tracked and thus not freed by ems_usb_close().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "the USB framework unanchors the URB before the complete function is called" and that completed in-URBs are "no longer anchored and ... not released in ems_usb_close()", while the patch fixes this by adding usb_anchor_urb(urb, &dev->rx_submitted) before usb_submit_urb() and usb_unanchor_urb(urb) on submit failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Track resubmitted RX URBs in the anchor list and unanchor them on submit failure to fix receive URB lifecycle management.
intent_record.what: In ems_usb_read_bulk_callback(), the resubmitted read URB is now anchored with usb_anchor_urb(urb, &dev->rx_submitted) before usb_submit_urb(), a successful submission immediately returns, and on submission failure the code now calls usb_unanchor_urb(urb); the error handling was also adjusted so that -ENODEV still detaches the net device while all other failures log an error through the else branch.
intent_record.how: This ensures each successfully resubmitted receive URB is tracked in dev->rx_submitted, allowing proper lifecycle management and cleanup of active RX URBs, while avoiding leaving a failed submission incorrectly anchored by explicitly unanchoring it. Runtime behavior changes by keeping successful resubmissions registered and preventing stale anchor state on submission errors.

grouping_result.intent: Track resubmitted RX URBs in the anchor list and unanchor them on submit failure to fix receive URB lifecycle management.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by re-anchoring resubmitted RX URBs so they remain tracked after USB core unanchors them on completion, and unanchoring on submit failure to maintain correct URB lifecycle and cleanup in ems_usb_close().

candidates.rationale: The callback resubmits the RX URB directly, but due to USB core behavior the URB has already been unanchored before completion handling. Resubmitting it without re-anchoring causes the driver to lose tracking of the URB, so ems_usb_close() cannot later find and free it.

vuln_statements.explanation: This resubmits the receive URB from the completion callback without first re-anchoring it. Because the USB core has already unanchored the URB before ems_usb_read_bulk_callback() runs, the resubmitted URB is no longer tracked on dev->rx_submitted, so ems_usb_close() cannot later kill/free it.

commit 702171adeed3607ee9603ec30ce081411e36ae42
Author: Sebastian Haas <haas@ems-wuensche.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 16 02:04:20 2009 +0000

    ems_usb: Added support for EMS CPC-USB/ARM7 CAN/USB interface
    
    This patch adds support for one channel CAN/USB interace CPC-USB/ARM7 from
    EMS Dr. Thomas Wuensche (http://www.ems-wuensche.com).
    
    Signed-off-by: Sebastian Haas <haas@ems-wuensche.com>
    Signed-off-by: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is visible in the provided function bodies. In ems_usb_start(), RX URBs are anchored once before first submission: `usb_anchor_urb(urb, &dev->rx_submitted);` followed by `err = usb_submit_urb(urb, GFP_KERNEL);`. However, in the RX completion handler `ems_usb_read_bulk_callback()`, after completion it directly reuses and resubmits the same URB via `usb_fill_bulk_urb(...)` and `retval = usb_submit_urb(urb, GFP_ATOMIC);` with no `usb_anchor_urb(urb, &dev->rx_submitted)` before resubmission. Given the root cause that the USB core unanchors a completed URB before the callback runs, this means the resubmitted RX URB is no longer tracked by `dev->rx_submitted`. Cleanup only kills anchored RX URBs in `unlink_all_urbs()` using `usb_kill_anchored_urbs(&dev->rx_submitted);`, so resubmitted-but-unanchored RX URBs would not be freed/stopped by close. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is absent because the callback does not re-anchor before resubmission.
